Hi Ranjit / Acme privacy team — thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can draft a scoped response and suggested contract language: 

Summary from our call:
- Acme: needs a clear delete (RTBF) workflow for user-initiated erase requests across primary store, caches, and backups.
- Target SLA: your product security team prefers evidence of completed deletions within 30 days, with attestations and audit logs.
- Residency: EU residency for EU customers and some EEA-specific handling.

Clarifying questions (so we scope the solution correctly):
1) PII scope — do you consider analytics/derived embeddings that contain user text as PII in scope for RTBF?
2) Backup constraints — you mentioned a backup window where immutable snapshots may retain data. Can you confirm whether a 90-day backup window is acceptable as a known exception?
3) Logging requirements — what level of audit evidence do you need? Token-level deletion events, per-user event with signature, or a periodic attestation?
4) Priority users — are any subsets (admins, subscribers) subject to different deletion rules?

Next steps I propose:
- If you confirm the answers above I’ll loop in our security lead Markus and our Solutions engineer Monica for a technical proposal and a short MPO (mutual plan of action) that includes timeline and the artifacts we’ll provide (audit logs, signed attestation, and sample export).
- If helpful, send over your current RTBF checklist or the PDF we discussed and we’ll annotate Redwoods’ mapping.

Attached: placeholder for your RTBF checklist if you shared during the call.

Best,

Hi Naomi — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers to your clarifying questions so you can begin drafting options: 

1) PII scope: We treat any content that can identify an end user (direct identifiers and unredacted user text) as in-scope. Derived artifacts (embeddings) are in scope if they can be reliably linked back to the user.

2) Backup window: Our legal & ops teams accept an explicit backup-exception if the vendor provides a reasonable plan for deletion from backups post-snapshot and an attendant attestation. Our preference is that primary stores be deleted within 30 days; backups are understood to be best-effort — we typically accept up to 90 days for immutable snapshots if documented.

3) Logging / evidence: We need per-request audit records that show the request id, user id, timestamp, and the downstream actions taken (soft-delete marker, hard-delete, artifact purged). A signed attestation at completion is also required for procurement.

4) Priority users: No special categories for now. If that changes we’ll flag you.

I’ve looped in our CISO (ciso@acmeinc.com) and privacy mailbox. Attached is our internal RTBF checklist — should help with mapping.

-Ranjit

Thanks for the ping and the context — happy to own the technical proposal. High-level response below (so you have language for the MPO and procurement one-pager): 

Technical capability and proposed offer:
- Primary stores (live DBs & caches): we can implement a per-request hard-delete workflow that removes user objects from the primary store within 24–72 hours of an approved erase request. We will also emit a per-request audit event (request_id, user_id, actor, timestamps, actions taken).

- Caches/KV: KV cache entries and prefix caches are evicted immediately on delete; we will include cache-eviction events in the audit trail.

- Immutable backups / snapshots: currently our deep cold snapshots are write-once and retained for compliance and operational restore. Practically, we can commit to a backup-exception policy: label snapshots with metadata so we can identify snapshots containing the user and schedule deletion/hard-purge on next retention cycle. Realistically, immutable snapshot purging will be completed within 90 days from the snapshot date; we cannot guarantee instant removal from existing immutable media.

- Evidence / attestation: we can produce per-request audit logs (CSV/JSON) and a signed attestation template stating the request was processed and backups have been scheduled for purge per the agreed retention window. We can also provide a short transcript showing the deletion events.

Suggested commercial construct (to present to Acme):
1) Offer: Primary data purged within 30 days; backups purged up to 90 days with documented exception.
2) Deliverables: per-request audit export (machine-readable), signed attestation at completion, and a one-page technical appendix mapping data types to storage tiers.
3) SLA / credit: If we miss the 90-day backup purge commitment, offer a pro-rated service credit for the month and a remediation plan.

Next actions I’ll take this afternoon:
- Draft the one-pager and attestation template.
- Prepare a short technical appendix mapping our storage tiers and timelines.
- Upload the draft to the shared Drive and create a DocuSign envelope for the attestation if you want a signature flow.

Monica — can you prepare a quick MPO with milestones (Draft MPO, Technical appendix, Attestation, Delivery) so Naomi can send to Ranjit?

-Markus
